newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 1996 debt, deficit inside EMU-limits - SF.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 1996 debt, deficit inside EMU-limits - SF.

text.p: Finland's gross public debt according to criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) was 58.8 percent of GDP at end-1996 and the EMU deficit was 2.6 percent, Statistics Finland said on Monday.
The debt entry limit for EMU is 60 percent and the deficit ceiling is 3.0 percent.
Finnish debt to GDP "was narrowly inside the convergence criterion for European economic and monetary union," SF said in a statement.

Of the 36 billion markka increase in state debt in 1996, work pension funds made up 21 billion markka, SF said. The holdings of state debt by work pension and other social security funds are excluded when calculating the gross public debt to GDP ratio for the third stage of EMU.
The deficit of the public sector finances relative to GDP "was inside the three percent criterion for the first time since 1991," SF said.

The state finances were 39 billion markka in the red last year, the municipal sector finances showed a surplus of four billion markka and social security funds were 21 billion markka in surplus, SF said.
